title: The Dice Game: Draupadi Questions the Wager
subtitle: A challenge to the claim made in the council hall

wager.author: traditionally attributed to Vyasa
wager.locator: Book IV · DYUTA; Book IV · DYUTA, normalized characters 2126-2309
wager.excerpt: Doth a crowned king and husband stake his wife and lose his queen, Did my noble lord and monarch sense and reason lose at dice, Other stake he did not wager, wedded wife to sacrifice!
wager.note: Verbatim English translation from Dutt. The Mahabharata volume is a condensed verse rendering; the Ramayana volume contains only the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam.

narrativeBlocks.title: A messenger brings the claim
narrativeBlocks.body: In Dutt's condensed verse rendering, a menial tells Draupadi that Yudhishthira lost a dice game and that Duryodhana claims her as a stake.

narrativeBlocks.title: Draupadi asks what was wagered
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Dutt's English rendering; whitespace normalized): “Doth a crowned king and husband stake his wife and lose his queen, Did my noble lord and monarch sense and reason lose at dice, Other stake he did not wager, wedded wife to sacrifice!”

narrativeBlocks.title: The question is about agency
narrativeBlocks.body: Draupadi asks whether a king who has lost himself can then stake his wife. The scene gives her a direct argument in the assembly.

narrativeBlocks.title: Abridged verse, not a full critical text
narrativeBlocks.body: Dutt's Maha-bharata is explicitly condensed into English verse. The local edition notes that it translates selected portions of the Sanskrit epic.

narrativeBlocks.title: The wager is contested
narrativeBlocks.body: The episode does not ask learners to accept the dice outcome as morally settled: Draupadi challenges the logic of the claim against her.
